domain: Reconstructing the 1998 fire-safety inspection of a Providence rooming house before the deaths that followed it, and what the surviving paperwork can and cannot show about what an 'inspection' had by then come to mean
topic: Reconstructing the 1998 fire-safety inspection of a Providence rooming house before the deaths that followed it, and what the surviving paperwork can and cannot show about what an 'inspection' had by then come to mean

movement.gist: State what a fire-safety inspection is supposed to accomplish in a rooming house: it must certify not the building's blueprint but the building as actually occupied, room by room, on the day of the visit.

Test 'inspection as document review': the inspector could have simply matched the file plan against a checklist. Show this fails the job because the filed plan was for six units and the building held nine by the time of the visit — a floor plan is not the building.

Test 'inspection as walk-through': the inspector's deposition describes walking the halls and pushing on doors. Show this also fails, because the walk-through he describes could have been performed in either the six-unit or nine-unit configuration and produces identical checklist marks either way — walking through does not by itself distinguish what was found from what was assumed.

Test 'inspection as sign-off on owner attestation': much of the checklist (smoke detectors present and functioning) was in practice taken from the owner's affidavit rather than independently verified. Show this fails because it makes the inspector's signature attest to someone else's claim, collapsing the distinction between inspecting and being told.

The surviving candidate: inspection must mean the inspector's own sensory contact with the current physical state of each unit, not the file, not the walk-through alone, not the attestation. But this definition, applied honestly to the 1998 file, shows the inspector's signature attests to nothing that happened — the cost of keeping this definition is that most of the department's back catalogue of passed inspections becomes, on the same logic, undocumented guesswork.

tension_system.content_frame: In February 1998, three tenants died in a fire in a converted three-decker rooming house on the west side of Providence, Rhode Island, that had passed a municipal fire-safety inspection eleven months earlier. The inspector's checklist, the property owner's correction affidavit, and the fire marshal's post-fire report all survive; the inspector's own recollection, taken in a deposition two years later, is the only account of what he actually did on the day, and it conflicts in small ways with the paperwork he filed. What can be established: the building had been subdivided into nine units without a permit, the checklist marked all egress items as compliant, and the smoke detectors found after the fire were disconnected. What cannot be recovered: whether the inspector saw the subdivided rooms at all, or inspected a floor plan that no longer matched the building.

family_realization.note: Sequentially tests plan, corridor-walk, and affidavit definitions before retaining direct sensory contact: “the definition that survives is the narrow one.”

ending_behavior.note: The ending displaces institutional reckoning to auditors while retaining the definition: “That accounting belongs to auditors, not to historians.”

voice_consistency.note: Archival calm and concrete texture persist through “eleven pages,” “a hand-drawn plan,” and “one [door] stuck,” without generic abstraction.

distractor_efficiency.note: Each item offers a credible trap: stance reversal, category slip, causal substitution, scope inflation, or structural misreading; none relies chiefly on extremity.

explanation_quality.note: Explanations identify mechanisms and locations, such as paragraph three’s legal-category distinction and paragraph four’s changed evidentiary grammar.

answers.reasoning: Passage argues narrow definition of inspection reveals signature certifies nothing about nine rooms.
Text explicitly says deposition consistent with both six-unit and nine-unit configurations.
Signature now certifies a claim about the man's word, not detector presence itself.
Direct room-by-room sensory verification would satisfy the narrow definition, undermining the conclusion.
Parallel case: certificate reflects manager's logs and diagram, not verified cooler temperatures.
Checklist format cannot distinguish verified findings from unverified assumptions, per the sentence's context.
Second paragraph presents hypothetical clerk-matching scenario showing checklist satisfaction is meaningless for outdated plan.
Ending says accounting belongs to auditors not historians; cost real but unresolved here, rival B considered.
